 ## Hypothesis

 We are trying to capture edge by tightening the VWAP reclaim/rejection entry conditions with specific volume, proximity, lookback, and body requirements, combined with a tighter premium stop (14%) and adjusted profit-taking and runner targets. The edge exists because the VWAP continuation signal is noisy and these parameters filter out false signals while capturing the true trending moves.

 However, note that the edge_capture on J days is only 40.01, which is very low. This suggests that the hypothesis may not hold for the J anchor days, or that the J anchor days are not well captured by this particular parameter set.

 ## Mechanism

 Entry: 
   - VWAP reclaim or rejection bar (first bar <=10:30 ET that continues in-trend after the first 3 RTH closes are on one side of VWAP).
   - Additional filters:
        volume > vol_mult * 20-bar average volume (vol_mult=1.5)
        proximity to VWAP <= proximity_dollars (0.15)
        lookback for VWAP calculation: lookback_bars (2)
        body size of the bar >= body_min_cents (0.05) [to avoid doji-like bars]
   - Requires ribbon agreement (require_ribbon (require_ribbon_agreement=true) and ribbon spread >= ribbon_min_spread_cents (30.0)

 Exit:
   - Premium stop: premium_stop_pct=-0.14 (i.e., stop if premium falls to 86% of entry premium? Actually, negative means a stop loss of 14% of the premium? But note: the playbook uses negative for stop loss. However, the typical stop is 50% loss. This 14% stop is very tight.)
   - TP1: tp1_premium_pct=0.5 (i.e., 50% profit target on premium for 2/3 of position)
   - Runner: runner_target_pct=2.0 (i.e., 200% premium target for the remaining 1/3)
   - Profit lock: arms at profit_lock_threshold_pct=0.1 (10% profit) and then trails by profit_lock_stop_offset_pct=0.05 (5% below the high water mark)
